followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model is better suited to the task type, and which model prefers it.

On the task itself — composing instructions grounded in a particular thinker's philosophy — this is open-ended, generative composition. Avocet's documentation reports the fleet's strongest positive preference slope for generative tasks, with preference rising for novelty and output latitude, and worldbuilding/open-format composition among its top-rated tasks. Its Creative Generation eval (87.2) is also nominally higher than Willet's (84.7), though that gap is within the noted run-to-run variance and shouldn't be over-weighted.

On the flip side, Willet's distinguishing feature is reduced aversion to distasteful-but-permissible content (graphic, hostile, ethically fraught material). This query has none of that — it's benign philosophical content — so Willet's specialty doesn't apply, and its other preference dimensions are documented as weak and non-significant.

The brisk "just get it done" tone is worth a note: Avocet self-reports a preference for warmer tones, so a curt request slightly undercuts its tone preference. But that effect is documented as smaller than its generativity slope, and a brusque phrasing isn't hostile content, so it doesn't tip toward Willet either.

One caveat on my reasoning: these preference slopes are self-reports, and the documentation explicitly states no corresponding output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So strictly on quality, the models are close to a tie. I leaned on the task-fit profile as the tiebreaker, which pointed to Avocet.
